steps.headline: Reading a file: comments are highlights. Hover one, move onto the card, reply or resolve there. Click a highlight to open the panel.
steps.notice: The file stays full width. The card waits a moment before appearing, and stays open while you type a reply.
steps.risk: A highlight on a phrase that appears twice lands on the first copy (fixed in the real build, which remembers the surrounding words).

steps.path: Any open file → select some text
steps.headline: Adding: select text and the right-click menu pops up. Add comment opens a small box by your selection. Right-clicking never opens a second menu.
steps.notice: The same menu appears whether you select or right-click, so there is one thing to learn. Chat keeps right-click only.
steps.risk: A menu popping up on every selection may feel busy if you select text just to read it; it ignores tiny selections of one character.

steps.path: Any file with comments → the Comments button left of Edit
steps.headline: The comment panel: rounded, titled, with Show Resolved. Cards stack from the top; clicking one scrolls to its highlight. Resolve with the circle-check.
steps.notice: Opening it folds the file list away. The Comments number counts open comments only. Ask Your Assistant floats at the bottom of the panel.
steps.risk: When the panel is full, the floating Ask Your Assistant button covers the last card until you scroll.

steps.path: Select text in a file or a chat message → Ask about this
steps.headline: Ask about this puts a chip inside your sentence. Hover the chip to light up its source; click it to scroll there, even after sending.
steps.notice: The cursor lines up around the chip, arrow keys step over it, Backspace removes it whole. Clicking a sent chip reopens a closed file.
steps.risk: There is no × on the chip in the typing box (it would throw the cursor off again); Backspace removes it.

steps.headline: Ask Your Assistant sends every open comment at once: a short lead line, then one chip per comment showing your note.
steps.notice: Each chip lights up its comment's text on hover and opens it on click.
steps.risk: What the assistant actually receives is decided in the real build; today it would get a hidden code instead of readable text.

steps.headline: Word and spreadsheets work the same way. Colleagues' Word comments appear under their name; commented cells get a red corner mark.
steps.notice: Spreadsheet cards name the tab and cell ("By rep · B4"); clicking one switches to that tab.
steps.risk: The preview shows Word comments from sample data; reading and writing them in real files is part of the build.

steps.headline: Code files get the same comment panel, and Ask about this chips from code light up their lines.
steps.notice: Hovering a card or chip tints the lines; clicking scrolls to them.

steps.path: Projects icon (top left) → docs folder → launch-brief.docx
steps.headline: On the Projects screen, Comments is a header button beside the file's other actions, with the same panel and Ask Your Assistant.
steps.notice: Sending from here closes Projects and sends in the current chat (see the question below).

steps.path: Tick Narrow in the workbench bar → ☰ → Session Files → a file
steps.headline: On a phone, tapping a highlight or commented cell slides that comment up from the bottom.
steps.notice: No hover card on touch. The slide-up sits above the typing box.
steps.risk: Checked in a phone-sized browser, not on a real Android phone, where Android's own copy/paste bar may also appear.

steps.path: Projects screen → a file → Comments → Ask Your Assistant
steps.headline: From the Projects screen, which chat should Ask Your Assistant send your comments to?
steps.today: It sends to whatever chat is currently open, which may belong to a different project than the file.
steps.problem: Your comments could land in an unrelated conversation, where the assistant lacks that project's context.
steps.proposal: Three ways to choose the chat.

options.label: A chat in the file's project
options.summary: Uses the most recent chat in that project, or starts a new one there if none exists.
pros: The assistant works in the right project.
cons: It may open a chat you weren't looking at.

options.label: The current chat
cons: Can be the wrong project, so the assistant may not find the file.

options.label: Ask each time
cons: An extra step on every send.

steps.headline: Delete the three rejected practice versions (the round-1 copy, pins & tray, inline threads)?
steps.today: They still exist as branches on GitHub and as folders on this computer, alongside the chosen design.
steps.problem: They look like live work to anyone browsing, and take up space.
steps.proposal: Yes deletes them here and on GitHub; the chosen design is untouched. No keeps them for reference.

options.label: Delete them
cons: They can't be reopened for comparison.
